summary: The all-empty placebo path is now handled correctly, but the guard does not cover every input that `abeclean` can reduce to no observations. Most importantly, files with usable values in only one name component—or only punctuation in the other—may still stop the pipeline with r(2000).

findings.title: The new guard still calls `abeclean` when one component contains no cleanable names
findings.what_the_code_does: The guard calls `abeclean` whenever `count if fs_namefrst!="" | fs_namelast!=""` is positive. Inside `abeclean`, however, each field is processed separately: characters outside `[a-z ]` are removed and then `split` is called on that field. Thus a file with all first names blank but at least one surname—or with raw nonempty strings that normalize entirely to empty—passes the outer guard while presenting an empty field to `split`, the same condition associated with r(2000).
findings.why_it_matters: The intended fix makes the placebo runnable but may still abort the substantive FamilySearch run for a birthplace where only one name component is populated or where apparent names contain no cleanable letters. Because the pipeline iterates over all birthplace files, one such file prevents production of the baseline link counts.
findings.how_to_check: In Stata, create a small dataset with `fs_namefrst=""`, `fs_namelast="smith"`, and `sex=1`, then run the exact `abeclean` call from line 70. Repeat with one component containing only punctuation such as `"."`. Confirm whether either case returns r(2000). Also tabulate, by divided file, whether each component has any value remaining after the normalization at abeclean.ado:157-173.
findings.suggested_fix: Test cleanability separately for each component after applying the same normalization as `abeclean`. Generate an empty cleaned output for a component with no usable tokens while safely cleaning the other component, or update and pin the repository copy of `abeclean` so its per-field loop explicitly handles an entirely empty component.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied. The untracked reports concern an older draft and were treated as review artifacts, not as the current paper; claims-vs-code could not be validated against manuscript text.
The external census data were unavailable, so the prevalence of files with only one populated or cleanable FamilySearch component could not be measured.
Stata was not available to execute the pipeline. The remaining r(2000) path is a source-level inference from the documented failure and `abeclean` implementation, hence confidence is marked likely.
The review target was the uncommitted working tree, not a new full-repository audit; unchanged dependencies were read only as needed to trace the modified branch.
